chapterInsights.title: Limits & Continuity
outcomes: Evaluate limits by substitution and factorisation
formulas: Continuity: f(a) defined, limit exists, and equals f(a)

f is continuous at a if all three conditions hold: defined, limit exists, limit=f(a).

Chapter-by-chapter teaching focus (derived from the module's own learning outcomes and key definitions):

• Chapter 1 — Limits & Continuity. Emphasise: Evaluate limits by substitution and factorisation; State conditions for continuity; Evaluate limits at infinity. Local context: Limits underpin marginal analysis — SA economists use calculus-based models for policy impact assessment.

• Chapter 2 — Derivatives & Differentiation Rules. Emphasise: Apply power, product, quotient and chain rules; Differentiate polynomial and composite functions. Local context: Marginal cost and revenue functions — core to SA business pricing decisions — are derivatives of TC and TR.

• Chapter 3 — Applications of Derivatives. Emphasise: Find critical points by setting f'(x)=0; Classify using second derivative test; Determine intervals of increase/decrease. Local context: SA managers use the second derivative test to confirm that a proposed production level truly maximises profit.

• Chapter 4 — Optimisation. Emphasise: Formulate and solve business optimisation problems; Find profit-maximising output; Minimise cost functions. Local context: SA firms in competitive markets face razor-thin margins — calculus-based profit optimisation is applied in financial modelling and pricing.

• Chapter 5 — Indefinite Integration. Emphasise: Find antiderivatives using the power rule; Apply the constant of integration; Recover TC from MC. Local context: Integrating MC gives TC — used in SA cost accounting and managerial economics for pricing decisions.

• Chapter 6 — Definite Integration. Emphasise: Evaluate definite integrals using the fundamental theorem; Interpret result as area under a curve; Calculate total revenue from MR. Local context: Definite integrals compute total revenue or total cost over an output range — standard in SA business analytics.

• Chapter 7 — Applications of Integration. Emphasise: Find area between two curves; Calculate consumer and producer surplus. Local context: Consumer/producer surplus analysis is used by SA Competition Commission to assess welfare effects of mergers and price controls.

Pedagogy tip (quantitative): work at least one fully solved example on the board per topic, then assign a parallel guided-practice problem. Common student errors: sign errors in debit/credit (accounting), confusing correlation with causation (stats/econ), and unit/percentage mistakes in ratio work.
